layman_headline: Portfolio holds three positions in a fearful market — patience is the play right now.
layman_explanation: The crypto market is in a 'Fear' state with Bitcoin struggling below $64K and losing its 200-week trend line. We currently hold SOL, LINK, and FET — all slightly underwater but well within their stop-loss ranges. The swing candidates on offer are either wildly overbought after massive pumps (AKE up 154%, BTW up 88%, VELVET up 69%) or are stablecoins with no trade potential. There's no compelling new entry that offers a clear risk-reward advantage over our current positions.
layman_action: Hold your current positions and wait. All three trades are near entry prices with intact stop-losses. Don't chase coins that have already pumped 50-150% in a week during a fearful market.
expert_reasoning: All three current positions (SOL -0.7%, LINK -0.5%, FET -2.8%) are marginally down but well above stop-losses. The swing candidates present a poor setup: AKE has RSI 91.7 (extreme overbought), H and VELVET just dropped 28-29% in 24h after massive weekly pumps (classic blow-off reversals), BTW lacks RSI/MACD data with an 88% weekly gain, and MON's RSI 39 pullback lacks any catalyst. BTC dominance at 56.3% continues to pressure alts. The Fear & Greed index at 31 is improving slightly (from 30.4 weekly avg), which could support a bounce in our existing positions. Adding a fourth position in this environment would increase risk without proportional reward.

$390M weekly ETF outflows signal institutional selling pressure that may accelerate
FET down 96.5% from ATH shows structural weakness — the -12.2% weekly decline could continue

LINK momentum — it's up 15.1% on the week with RSI still neutral at 49, closest to profit target of our three positions
Fear & Greed index trend — currently improving from 30.4 to 31, a move above 35 could signal alt relief rally
market_context: Bitcoin at $63,550 has lost its 200-week trend line with $390M in weekly ETF outflows, creating a cautious backdrop. BTC dominance at 56.3% and Fear & Greed at 31 ('Fear') suggest this is not the time to add risk — but improving sentiment trend offers hope for existing positions.
context_banner: Market in Fear with BTC losing key long-term support — hold existing positions with tight stop-losses while waiting for clarity.

Fear & Greed at 31 (Fear) but slightly improving from 30.4 weekly average — not yet signaling capitulation or recovery, keeping us in wait mode.
AKE RSI at 91.7 and MON RSI at 39.1 represent the two extremes among candidates — neither offers a clean swing setup with defined catalysts.
Bitcoin ETF outflows of $390M for the week indicate institutional caution and remove a key demand driver for near-term price support.
No volume breakout patterns detected among viable candidates — the pumped coins (AKE, BTW, VELVET) show momentum exhaustion rather than sustainable breakouts.
